Transhumance
Two Types of Transhumance
•   fixed: mainly in countries with predictable seasons, e.g. Switzerland
•   nomadic: in areas with unpredictable climatic conditions, e.g. Somalia
Study on the Movement of Pastoralists
•   For fixed transhumance, the pattern of movement is described as .
•   While for nomadic transhumance, the pattern is more complex and varied.

Number of People Involved
•   For fixed transhumance, only pastoralists make the journey.
•   However, all nomadic transhumance migrate with their livestock.

analyses.content: 听到录音提到研究者看重牧民的行进路线时，紧接着就明确指出了这种固定模式被称为vertical。
你可能会因为只听到后面的“lower/higher ground”而忽略了前面直接给出的答案，要注意听“known as”这类直接引出定义的信号词。

Secondly, researchers sometimes look at the type of journey that pastoralists make, their movement. For fixed transhumance, the pattern is sometimes known as vertical because it typically consists of a journey from lower ground in the winter season to higher ground in the summer, and vice versa.
录音提到固定模式的住所时，明确举例说明了山区里的半永久避难所比如cabin（小木屋）。
你可能会被前面的“permanent homes”干扰，一定要抓住题干中的“semi-permanent”和对应“high ground”的“mountains”来锁定最终答案。

Another distinction is sometimes made in terms of homes. In the case of fixed transhumance, the group will typically have permanent homes in the valley and a shelter which is semi-permanent in the mountains, such as a cabin, to offer some protection from the weather.
录音以Gabra牧民为例，明确指出他们把房屋框架背在camel（骆驼）上。
你可能会在听到“livestock”（牲畜）时就急于填词，要注意题目问的是Gabra人的具体例子，需耐心听到具体的动物名称。

In nomadic transhumance, however, the pastoralists always live in temporary shelters which are transported by their livestock from place to place and are usually light and portable. In northern Kenya, for example, the Gabra pastoralist carries the frame of his home on his camel and then covers it with branches when he stops for the night.
录音提到人数的区别时指出，只有负责照看牧群的人去迁徙，而这些人通常是young（年轻的）人。
你可能听到了“only the people”就去寻找某种特定职业，要注意紧跟在后面的补充说明句才是真正描述人群特征的答案句。

A 4th factor often mentioned is the number of people taking part. In the case of fixed transhumance, only the people who actually look after the herds travel. These are normally the young ones because they can withstand adverse physical conditions more easily.
录音明确指出，那些不离开山谷的人通常会开始作为farmers（农民）来工作并耕种土地。
你可能会听到“cultivating the land”但不知道对应的身份词，要注意紧跟在“working as”信号词后面的职业名称。
The last points of comparison often made by researchers are diet and goods. In fixed transhumance, those who do not move from the valleys often start working as farmers, cultivating the land.
听到与外界社区建立联系时，录音紧接着说他们会用动物来交易grain（谷物）。
你可能会对“trade”和题干中“exchange”的同义替换不敏感，导致听到了animals却错过了后面的换取物。
They build up contacts with other communities, and in some cases, they may also trade animals for grain.
录音总结游牧模式满足自身所有需求时，具体列举了他们从畜群中获取食物以及clothing（衣服）。
你可能会被奶酪和肉这两个具体的细节干扰，而忽略了题干“food and ___”所需要的并列大类概念词。

In nomadic transhumance, there are fewer contacts. The group are generally regarded as providers of all their own needs, and they obtain food such as cheese and meat and also their clothing from their herds.
录音明确指出他们传统上会帮助当地农民进行harvest（收割）。
你可能会对“assisted”和题干“help”的同义替换反应慢半拍，导致跟丢答案出现的位置。
They have traditionally assisted local farmers with the harvest, which takes place while they are temporarily a resident there.
录音提到住所时，直接说明他们住在tents（帐篷）里，并补充这些住所是临时的。
你可能会觉得答案太明显而犹豫，记住听到“live in”这种直接的地点/住所提示就该立刻捕捉名词。
It is true they live in tents, and these are movable and temporary right through the year, whether they are in the Sahara or in the north of Algeria.
录音总结这种同时具备两种特征的游牧类型时，给出了更精确的称呼即intermediate（中间型）。
你可能会没有反应过来“more precisely refer to as”完全对应题干的“A better term to describe”，一定要注意捕捉总结性的学术定义词。
Here, in fact, we have a case showing some features of both types of transhumance, which we might more precisely refer to as intermediate.
